/networks/tron.title: When a transfer needs a closer look

questions.q: Can USDT pay the TRON network fee?
questions.a: Oath’s ordinary TRC-20 send flow uses TRON resources, with TRX charges when resources are insufficient. Holding USDT alone does not guarantee you can send it. Recipient account requirements can also affect the estimate.

questions.q: Why is my token balance available but Send cannot continue?
questions.a: A token balance and the network fee balance are separate. Check that TRX is available on TRON, then read Oath’s estimate and any account requirements. A balance on another network cannot pay this transaction’s fee.

questions.q: The sender says it is complete. Where is my transfer?
questions.a: Ask for the public transaction ID and the exact network. Check the destination and token identifier in that network’s explorer. A withdrawal request is not the same as a confirmed on-chain transfer. If the explorer confirms the correct transfer, refresh the matching account in Oath.

questions.q: What if I selected the wrong network?
questions.a: Stop and check the original transaction before sending again. A matching address is not proof of recovery. Contact the receiving service for its supported recovery process; never provide recovery credentials to support.

/networks/bitcoin.title: Match your Bitcoin account and address

questions.q: Which Bitcoin address should I use?
questions.a: Choose a format supported by both the sender and your imported wallet. Taproot, Native SegWit, wrapped SegWit and Legacy are Bitcoin address choices, not different coins. The choices available in Oath depend on your recovery material.

questions.q: Why does my receiving address change?
questions.a: A supported Bitcoin account can derive multiple receiving and change addresses. Compare an earlier address and its transaction history when checking recovery; a new receiving address alone does not establish an account mismatch.

questions.q: Can I receive a Lightning payment here?
questions.a: This guide is for on-chain BTC. A Lightning invoice, Bitcoin Cash address or wrapped BTC token is a different destination or asset.

/tokens/usdt.title: Choose the route before sharing an address

questions.q: Which network should I choose?
questions.a: Use a network supported by both the sender and the receiving account. Open its exact token page, compare the contract or mint, and check the fee asset for a later send. A lower advertised withdrawal fee does not establish compatibility.

questions.q: Are all versions and bridges equivalent?
questions.a: No. Entries are grouped by the catalog’s asset ID. Compare the exact identity with current issuer information. A familiar symbol does not prove issuance, redemption eligibility or bridge backing.

questions.q: What should I check after revoking?
questions.a: Read the transaction outcome and refresh Token access. A pending or failed operation is not a confirmed removal. Discovery can be partial or delayed, and some account-control entries are outside ordinary token revocation.

questions.q: Should I also disconnect the dApp?
questions.a: Review the WalletConnect session separately. Disconnecting stops that session’s future requests; it does not cancel an on-chain allowance. Revocation and session management solve different problems.

/features/icloud-wallet-backup.title: Check recovery before you need it

questions.q: The file is listed, but restore does not complete. What next?
questions.a: Use the Apple Account that holds the file and the password for that specific backup. An app passcode or passkey does not decrypt the backup. Follow the troubleshooting guide and preserve the original recovery material.

questions.q: Will every wallet format use this backup route?
questions.a: No. Check the supported scope above. Electrum and aezeed wallets are excluded in this reviewed release. Preserve their original recovery material and use the matching recovery guide.

/features/walletconnect.title: When a dApp will not connect

questions.q: The dApp shows only browser-extension wallets. Can Oath connect?
questions.a: The dApp needs a compatible WalletConnect or mobile app-link flow. Oath cannot make an extension-only connection option work. Check the dApp’s supported mobile wallets and exact network.

questions.q: Does connecting permit every future transaction?
questions.a: A session and a signing request have separate reviews. Read the website, account, network and requested action each time. Disconnect a session you no longer use and review token approvals separately.
